project_spec.name: Tsugi (次)
project_spec.overview: Tsugi (次) is a fast, edge-ready web app for building and sharing curated anime and manga lists. A signed-in user creates a named, categorised list of titles — found by searching a provider or imported from their own AniList/MyAnimeList library — scores and comments on them, and publishes a shareable link with a rich social preview. Anyone can open a published link; only creating requires an account. Published lists also appear on a public feed ranked by upvote/downvote score and filterable by category.

goals.goal: Zero-friction creation: from landing page to a share link on the clipboard in under 10 seconds.
Instant sharing: the link is auto-copied on publish, with one-click share buttons for X, Discord, and WhatsApp.
Rich previews: every public list URL renders a 1200x630 social card when pasted anywhere online.
Public discovery: a feed of published lists, vote-ranked and category-filterable.

out_of_scope.item: Comments and replies on lists — voting is the only social signal.
Per-user profile pages beyond a username shown on a feed entry.
Analytics dashboards, editing history, moderation tooling.

tech_stack.styling: Tailwind CSS 4 — configured in CSS, with no `tailwind.config.ts` — plus shadcn/ui components on Radix primitives
tech_stack.api_layer: Hono, mounted as a catch-all at `/api/[[...route]]`
tech_stack.database: PostgreSQL (Supabase), Drizzle ORM and drizzle-kit migrations, transaction pooler with prepared statements disabled
tech_stack.authentication: Better-Auth, mounted inside the Hono app, with OAuth against AniList and MyAnimeList
tech_stack.validation: Zod, applied at every API boundary via `@hono/zod-validator`
tech_stack.data_providers: AniList GraphQL API; MyAnimeList via the Jikan REST API and the official MAL API v2
tech_stack.ci: GitHub Actions running, in order: `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint .`, `bun test --conditions=react-server`

data_model.table: Better-Auth user fields, plus `username` (assigned a default at signup, editable in settings, unique) and `scoreFormat` (the scale the user rates on, captured at sign-in and refreshed whenever their tracker library is fetched).
Better-Auth OAuth accounts, holding provider access and refresh tokens. Server-read only.

`id` (uuid), `slug` (varchar 12, unique — the only public identifier), `name` (varchar 80, required — the user-chosen category, e.g. "Romance"), `caption` (varchar 120, optional), `comment` (varchar 280, optional), `views` (integer, default 0), `published` (boolean, default false), `publishedAt` (timestamp, nullable), `userId` (not null, FK to user), `createdAt`. Indexed on `userId` and on `(published, publishedAt)`.

`id`, `listId` (FK, cascade delete), `position` (integer — explicit ordering, never rely on insertion order), `provider` (enum: anilist | mal), `mediaType` (enum: anime | manga), `externalId`, `title`, `coverImage`, `score` (nullable), `scoreFormat` (nullable), `comment` (varchar 280, nullable).
`userId` + `listId` unique together, `value` (+1 or -1), `createdAt`. One vote per user per list; changing a vote updates the row.
Per-user cached copy of a fetched tracker library, keyed by `(userId, provider, mediaType)`, storing the entries as JSON with a fetch timestamp.
data_model.rule: Enable row-level security on every table. The database is exposed through a public REST endpoint by default; a table without RLS is a writable public API that bypasses all validation, rate limiting, and server-side logic.

api_surface.route: Create a list. Zod-validated. Rate-limited per user.
The session user's own lists, newest first.
Read one list owned by the session user.
Delete the list and its items.

Import the signed-in user's own library from a tracker. Serves the cached copy unconditionally; `?refresh=1` forces a live re-fetch, and if that fetch fails it falls back to the existing cache marked stale rather than erroring.
Published lists, vote-ranked, paginated, optionally filtered by category.
Distinct categories present in the feed, for filter chips.
Cast or change a vote. Requires a session. Rate-limited per user.

screens.screen: Landing page and, when signed in, the entry point to the list builder.
OAuth sign-in with AniList and MyAnimeList.
The public feed: slot-numbered published lists, category filter chips, vote controls, pagination.
The signed-in user's lists, with live/draft status, share, and delete.
Username editing and connected-provider management, including unlinking (never the last remaining provider).
The public list page. No session required. Fire-and-forget view counting.
A 1200x630 PNG social card: cover art, list name, item count, score, author, and Tsugi branding.

invariants.rule: Slugs are the only public identifier. Database ids never appear in a URL, an API response, or rendered HTML.

Provider JSON is converted to a single unified media type at the adapter boundary and never escapes it. Media is identified by the triple `(provider, mediaType, externalId)`, never by id alone: AniList and MyAnimeList id spaces are disjoint, so resolving an id against the wrong provider returns a different title or nothing. `provider` names the id space (`anilist` | `mal`), not the API vendor that answered — Jikan and the official MAL API both return `mal` ids.
There is no cross-provider fallback, because ids do not translate between providers.
The ORM never escapes the server. Database modules are importable only by server code; a component importing the ORM is always a bug.
Every API input is validated at the Hono boundary with a Zod schema. No hand-rolled JSON parsing.

Every visual value comes from a semantic design token (`bg-background`, `text-foreground`, `bg-primary`, …). No raw hex, no `rgb()`, no arbitrary Tailwind values in components. The palette is authored once, in the global stylesheet, and nowhere else.

A score is a `(raw, format)` pair, never a bare number. Supported formats: `POINT_100`, `POINT_10_DECIMAL`, `POINT_10`, `POINT_5`, `POINT_3` (smileys — it has no numeric rendering). A number without its format is meaningless. `0` means "unrated", not a score: every format floors at 1, and an imported `0` stores as `(null, null)`.
Comments are at most 280 characters, at both list and item level, enforced in the Zod schema, the database column, and the input control — all three, every time.
A list must say something: at least one score or one comment, at list or item level.
Creating requires a session; viewing never does. The public list page and its social card must stay open to anonymous visitors, or the product has no distribution.
Provider access tokens never reach the client. They are read server-side only, never returned by an API route, never embedded in HTML, never logged.
Nothing without a timeout blocks the create flow. Every outbound provider call has an explicit timeout and a defined failure behaviour.
`params` and `searchParams` are always awaited, including in the social-card route.
Public reads must not require the database to be writable. View counting is fire-and-forget and may never block or fail a render.
Anything that touches the database runs on the Node runtime — the Postgres driver needs TCP, which the Edge runtime does not have. This includes the social-card route.
Rate limiting on write paths keys on the user, not the IP, since creating already requires a session.

code_standards.rule: TypeScript strict. No `any`, no non-null assertions, no `@ts-ignore`.
Secrets are referenced only in server and database modules. Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_`-prefixed variables may appear in client code.
Prefer shadcn components over hand-written equivalents; once added they are project source and are edited in place, not wrapped.
Add `"use client"` only where a hook or event handler needs it, and to the smallest component possible.
Schema changes go through generated migration files committed to the repository — never ad-hoc DDL.
Every mechanically-checkable requirement becomes a test in the same change that introduces it.

build_order.step: Scaffold: Next.js + Tailwind 4 + shadcn, environment validation, CI running typecheck, lint, and tests.
Data layer: Drizzle schema for all tables above, migrations, RLS on every table.
Authentication: Better-Auth inside Hono, AniList and MAL OAuth (MAL requires a custom PKCE token exchange), sign-in and settings screens, username assignment.
Media providers: unified media type, AniList and Jikan search adapters with timeouts and caching.
API surface: the Hono routers above, Zod validation, slug generation with collision retry, rate limiting.
Create and share UX: search, item tray, ordering, scoring, comments, publish, share modal with auto-copy.
Library import: token lookup and refresh, AniList and MAL list fetchers, per-user cache with explicit refresh, the import picker UI.
Dashboard: the user's lists with status, share, delete, and provider unlinking.
Feed: vote-ranked published lists, category filtering and discovery, vote controls.
